definitions.explanation: An immensely long, essentially endless span of time, originally from Buddhist cosmology (kalpa). In modern Japanese it almost always appears in the set phrase {未来永劫|みらいえいごう}.

examples.japanese: {未来永劫|みらいえいごう}⟦{忘|わす}れない→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧。
examples.english: I'll never forget — not for all eternity.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{約束|やくそく}→約束：01517_yakusoku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{未来永劫|みらいえいごう}⟦{変|か}わらない→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧。
examples.english: This promise will never change, for all time to come.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{業績|ぎょうせき}→業績：04873_gyouseki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{未来永劫|みらいえいごう}⟦{語|かた}り{継|つ}がれる→語り継ぐ：22312_kataritsugu⟧だろう。
examples.english: His achievements will be told for generations to come.

notes:
Originally a Buddhist term derived from the Sanskrit kalpa. In contemporary use it is virtually fixed to the four-character compound {未来永劫|みらいえいごう} 'for all future eternity', often appearing in formal or emphatic statements.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {未来永劫|みらいえいごう}: for all eternity to come (by far the most common form)
- {永劫|えいごう}⟦{回帰|かいき}→回帰：12061_kaiki⟧: eternal recurrence (philosophical term)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{永遠|えいえん}→永遠：01873_eien⟧: eternity — the everyday word; less formal and used much more broadly
- ⟦{永久|えいきゅう}→永久：01875_eikyuu⟧: permanence; forever — common in mechanical and legal senses (⟦{永久磁石|えいきゅうじしゃく}→永久磁石：25187_eikyuujishaku⟧)
